# The field guide, compact (CodyNote 0.48.0 and later)

One recipe per field, one line each here. **For field X, follow its recipe**: before writing a field, call `codynote_recipe(id)` for the whole recipe (where to look in order and what to look for in each, what counts as evidence and what does not, every rule, the checks before writing); `codynote_recipe(tab: "<tab>")` gives a tab. The update brief carries the same one line per field. The owner reads the full guide in docs/field-guide.md.

## Rules for every field

- Is it still true: CodyNote (the newest meeting and lines) → Fathom for a call not in CodyNote yet → Outlook email with the people on it → Teams chats → HubSpot (everything new: tickets, notes, emails, calls, meetings, tasks, quotes, deals); the web only for company facts.
- Never stop for an approval: suggest everything in one pass; the owner approves each suggestion in CodyNote.
- Never over what the owner typed: a box the owner set stays theirs until they clear it.
- Lengths: item title ≤ 90 characters; Next step ≤ 120 (who, what, and when only if a source says or implies it); storyline one-liner ≤ 90, no dates; Goal and Done when one sentence ≤ 300; Now 1–3 sentences ≤ 600; an item’s Situation three labeled parts ≤ 1,200; the read’s Situation ≤ 1,500 and its Do first one sentence ≤ 300.
- Items (0.53.0): one item per topic. A title is "Topic: what exactly, how much, for whom" (the owner’s short topic first, no "do this" verb, no ids or dates, no bare first name); the step is the Next step. A new item carries Situation (The ask: / Where it stands: / Why it matters:), Done when and Next step; Goal is no longer written. Picking (item.pick): fold into the open item on the topic first; others’ tasks that block the owner are a follow-up "waiting on ⟨name, role⟩".
- Priority: P1 = blocks a renewal, an outage, or the customer said urgent; P2 = due this week; P3 = a later date; P4 = nice to have, no date.
- Done needs proof (an email, a ticket note, a later call, a deal stage); without it the item stays open with a Context line saying what was checked.
- Made-up names only in examples; a field no source speaks to stays blank.

## Meetings (`meetings`)

Company › Meetings. The calls are where almost everything else comes from: Claude reads them first and changes only a meeting's date, title or kind. The rest of a meeting is what Fathom or the owner put there.

- **Meeting date** `meeting.held_on`: The day the call happened. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD, the owner’s local day, never in the future. (≤10; passes "2025-11-04", fails "Nov 4": no year and not YYYY-MM-DD) **Look:** Fathom → Outlook → CodyNote → HubSpot. **Never:** Never today as a default: no source with the call's own date, no change. **Write:** `meeting.held_on`
- **Meeting title** `meeting.title`: How the owner finds the call again in the list and in search. **Format:** Company, what the meeting was, and the month and day: "<Company> <kind words> - <Month Day>". 1 to 300 characters. (≤300; passes "Acme Q3 QBR + Roadmap - October 21", fails "Impromptu Zoom Meeting": says neither the company nor what the call was) **Look:** Fathom → Outlook → CodyNote. **Never:** Never rename a title only for style: only a misleading one (wrong company, "Impromptu Zoom Meeting", a QBR called a call) becomes "<Company> <what it was> - <Month Day>"; a fine title worded differently is left alone (owner, 2026-11-01). **Write:** `meeting.title`
- **Meeting kind** `meeting.kind`: Decides the last QBR and last roadmap the account row shows, the qbr signal on the book (over 120 days is a nudge) and where "since the last QBR" counts from. **Format:** One of: qbr, ebr, roadmap, qbr_roadmap, call, team, other. (≤11; passes "qbr_roadmap", fails "qbr": for a session whose agenda covered both the quarterly review and the roadmap: a joint session is qbr_roadmap, so the last roadmap moves too) **Look:** CodyNote → Fathom → Outlook. **Never:** Never team for a meeting with the customer on it, and never a customer kind for an internal call. **Write:** `meeting.kind`
- **Which Fathom recording to bring in (import)** `meeting.recording`: Inside an import Claude picks which Fathom calls belong to the account; CodyNote fetches each one itself. **Format:** codynote_import_meeting(import_id, ref, recording_id): the recording id as Fathom gives it, and a short ref (m1, m2...) for later changes to name. (≤60; passes "recording_id 81234567, ref m3", fails "the transcript text pasted as the meeting": Claude never carries a transcript; CodyNote fetches it by id) **Look:** CodyNote → Fathom. **Never:** Never paste a transcript or summary through the reply or a suggestion. **Write:** `tool:codynote_import_meeting`

**Never written by Claude:** Transcript and where it came from (`meeting.transcript`, the app works it out); Meeting notes (`meeting.notes`, owner only); Attendees (as written) (`meeting.attendees_text`, owner only); Recording link (`meeting.recording_url`, the app works it out); Which account a meeting is on (`meeting.company`, owner only); Fathom’s action items on a meeting (`meeting.fathom_items`, owner only).

## Documents and email (`documents`)

Company › Documents (files, links and the Email references). Email is a source, never a copy: one reference per email (who, when, subject, a one-line gist, a link to open it), read only when the owner asks. Files and links are the owner's.

- **Email reference: the message id (the whole window)** `email.message_id`: One reference per email in the window, worth it or not, so the index is complete and "did we ever email about X" has an answer. **Format:** The connector's message id exactly as it comes back (the id in mail:///messages/{id}); conversation_id as given. (≤1000; passes "AAMkAGI2TG93AAA=", fails "Re: FY27 renewal quote": a subject, not the message id) **Look:** Outlook → CodyNote. **Never:** Only when the owner asked for email: "catch up on email for Acme", "with email", an import, or an email-mode refresh (contradiction 14). Checking open action items reads Outlook every time without saving references (0.54.0). **Write:** `email.message_id`, `email.conversation_id`
- **Email subject** `email.subject`: How the owner recognises the thread in the list and in search. **Format:** The subject as received, trimmed. (≤1000; passes "Re: FY27 renewal quote", fails "Renewal quote discussion (cleaned up)": not the subject as sent) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Never reworded. **Write:** `email.subject`
- **Email sender (address and name)** `email.from`: Who wrote it: it sets the contact's last emailed date and tells the owner's own sent mail (an address on the owner's domains) from the customer's. **Format:** An email address (lower case) and the display name as given. (≤320; passes "dana.whitfield@example.com, Dana Whitfield", fails "Dana from IT": no address) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Never invent an address. **Write:** `email.from_address`, `email.from_name`
- **Email recipients** `email.to`: Everyone it went to (To and Cc): it gives each contact their last emailed date and shows who the owner keeps in the loop. **Format:** A list of {address, name}, each address once, at most 500. (≤2000; passes "[{address: "sam.ortiz@example.com", name: "Sam Ortiz"}]", fails "[{address: "IT team"}]": not an address) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Only when the owner asked for email: "catch up on email for Acme", "with email", an import, or an email-mode refresh (contradiction 14). Checking open action items reads Outlook every time without saving references (0.54.0). **Write:** `email.to`
- **Email sent time** `email.sent_at`: When it was sent: the date every History line, Observation and follow-up cut from this email carries, and what moves the watermark. **Format:** An ISO instant with its zone, as the connector gives it. (≤40; passes "2026-10-27T16:42:00Z", fails "last Tuesday": not a time) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Only when the owner asked for email: "catch up on email for Acme", "with email", an import, or an email-mode refresh (contradiction 14). Checking open action items reads Outlook every time without saving references (0.54.0). **Write:** `email.sent_at`
- **Email folder** `email.folder`: Inbox or sent: sent mail with no reply is what becomes a waiting tag. **Format:** inbox, sent, or the folder name as given. (≤200; passes "sent", fails "important": not a folder) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Only when the owner asked for email: "catch up on email for Acme", "with email", an import, or an email-mode refresh (contradiction 14). Checking open action items reads Outlook every time without saving references (0.54.0). **Write:** `email.folder`
- **Email link** `email.web_link`: Opens the email in Outlook from CodyNote: the reference points, the mailbox holds it. **Format:** An https link up to 4,000 characters, only as the connector gave it. (≤4000; passes "https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?ItemID=AAMkAGI2&exvsurl=1", fails "mail:///messages/AAMkAGI2": not an https link) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Never a made-up link; leave it out if the connector gave none. **Write:** `email.web_link`
- **Email gist** `email.gist`: One line in Claude’s words of what the email says, so search and the brief can find it without opening the mailbox ("is there anything about the Denver quote?"). **Format:** One line, at most 200 characters: who did what, with the number or date if there is one. (≤200; passes "Dana asks for the 50 TB Collab quote before the Jan 12 budget meeting.", fails "Email about the renewal.": says nothing the subject doesn’t) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Never a body pasted or paraphrased at length; never personal details unrelated to the account. **Write:** `email.gist`
- **Email matched by** `email.matched_by`: Says whether a known contact is on the email or only the domain: a domain-only email may name someone new. **Format:** contact or domain. (≤7; passes "contact", fails "name": not one of the two values) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never matched to an address on the owner’s own domains. **Write:** `email.matched_by`
- **Email read through (the watermark)** `email_sync.emails_through`: How far email has been read for the account, so the next catch-up starts there and nothing is read twice or skipped. **Format:** An ISO instant; only ever forward. (≤60; passes "2026-10-27T16:42:00Z", fails "2026-10-31": today’s date, not the newest email read) **Look:** Outlook. **Never:** Never moved by a partial search. **Write:** `email_sync.emails_through`

**Never written by Claude:** Document name (`document.name`, owner only); A link on the account (`document.url`, owner only); Document note (hidden) (`document.note`, owner only); Document text (read by the app) (`document.text`, the app works it out).

## People (`people`)

Company › Contacts, and each person’s profile page. Who is on the account, what part they play, and what the owner should know before the next call with them. One person, one card, on every account they are on.

- **Contact name** `contact.name`: Who the person is: every attendee match, speaker name, profile line and email match hangs off the contact. **Format:** First and last name as the person writes it, 1 to 300 characters; no title or company in the name. (≤300; passes "Dana Whitfield", fails "Dana (IT, Acme)": the title and company belong in their own boxes, and the last name is missing) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, email references) → HubSpot → Outlook (email threads) → Web. **Never:** Never a second contact for someone already in CodyNote: link them. **Write:** `contact.name`
- **Job title** `contact.title`: What they do: it tells the owner who to bring a renewal, a technical problem or a budget question to, and it often hints at the persona. **Format:** The title as they write it, up to 200 characters. (≤200; passes "Director of IT Infrastructure", fails "probably the storage person": a guess, not a title) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads) → CodyNote (meetings) → Web. **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `contact.title`
- **Email address** `contact.email`: How CodyNote matches their email and calls to them: the email recipe searches by it, and the duplicate guard uses it. **Format:** One email address, lower case, up to 320 characters. (≤320; passes "dana.whitfield@example.com", fails "dwhitfield@ (guessed)": not a full address, and a guess) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads) → CodyNote. **Never:** Never a guessed address. **Write:** `contact.email`
- **Mobile phone** `contact.mobile_phone`: How to reach them fast before a renewal or an outage. **Format:** As written, up to 100 characters. (≤100; passes "+1 303 555 0142", fails "call her cell": no number) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `contact.mobile_phone`
- **Direct phone** `contact.direct_phone`: Their own desk line. **Format:** As written, up to 100 characters. (≤100; passes "+1 303 555 0177 x204", fails "ext. on website": no number) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `contact.direct_phone`
- **Office phone** `contact.office_phone`: The office or main line they give. **Format:** As written, up to 100 characters. (≤100; passes "+1 303 555 0100", fails "see HubSpot": no number) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `contact.office_phone`
- **LinkedIn** `contact.linkedin_url`: Their background and moves at a glance before a first call. **Format:** An http(s) link up to 2,000 characters. (≤2000; passes "https://www.linkedin.com/in/dana-whitfield-example", fails "linkedin.com/search?q=Dana": a search, not their profile) **Look:** HubSpot → Web. **Never:** Never a profile that only matches the name. **Write:** `contact.linkedin_url`
- **Partner organisation** `contact.partner_org`: Which reseller, integrator or MSP a partner contact works for: it keeps partner people apart from the customer’s, and the duplicate guard matches the same name at the same partner org. **Format:** The partner’s name as the owner writes it, up to 200 characters. (≤200; passes "Northwind Partners", fails "reseller": not a name) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads) → CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never set on a customer’s own staff. **Write:** `contact.partner_org`
- **Customer or partner** `contact.kind`: Puts the person in the customer table or the Partners panel. **Format:** customer or partner. (≤8; passes "partner", fails "reseller": not one of the two values) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never change a customer to partner without a domain or signature that shows it. **Write:** `contact.kind`
- **Persona** `contact.role`: Their part in the account: it orders Key people on the Overview and tells the owner who sells for Panzura inside, who signs and who stands in the way. **Format:** One of: champion (sells Panzura inside when the owner isn’t there), economic_buyer (owns the budget, signs), technical_buyer (judges whether it works), decision_maker (makes the final call), executive_sponsor (senior backer, at EBRs), coach (tells the owner how decisions get made, doesn’t sell for us), user (uses it, no buying part), blocker (works against Panzura or the renewal), admin (runs the CloudFS environment), billing (POs, invoices), partner (a partner’s person), other. (≤17; passes "economic_buyer", fails "champion": for someone whose only evidence is one friendly call: a champion is shown by selling for us, not by being nice) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never set from a title alone. **Write:** `contact.role`
- **Reports to** `contact.reports_to_contact_id`: Who their boss is: the escalation path, and who the owner should meet next. **Format:** Another contact of the account, by contact id (a ref for one added in the same call); null when not known. (≤36; passes "c2", fails "Lee (not a contact yet)": must be a contact: add Lee with ref c2 and point at c2) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never a person on another account. **Write:** `contact.reports_to_contact_id`
- **Still there** `contact.active`: Someone who retired, left or changed role drops out of Key people, Who’s who and the email search, so the owner stops writing to a dead inbox and asks who replaced them. **Format:** false when they are no longer at the account; true when they come back. (≤5; passes "false", fails "no": true or false only) **Look:** Outlook (email threads) → CodyNote (meetings) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never inactive without a quote that says so. **Write:** `contact.active`
- **Really a different person** `contact.new_person`: Keeps an add an add when CodyNote would turn it into a link to someone with the same email or name at the same partner org. **Format:** true, on the add only. (≤4; passes "true", fails "yes": true only) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never used to force a duplicate of the same person. **Write:** `contact.new_person`
- **Put someone on this account too** `contact.link`: One person, one card: a partner’s account executive who covers three accounts, or an IT lead shared by sister companies, is linked to each instead of copied. **Format:** {action: link, record: contact, id: <their person_id>, company: <this account>}. (≤120; passes "link person 3f2a9c10 to Acme Engineering", fails "add Sam Ortiz again on Acme": a second card for one person) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never link a teammate. **Write:** `contact:link`
- **Merge copies of one person** `contact.merge`: Two cards for one person split their meetings, lines and emails; merging puts everything on the one kept. **Format:** {action: merge, record: contact, id: <the copy to keep>, fields: {merge_ids: [the others]}}. (≤160; passes "merge 9b1c0d22 into 3f2a9c10 (same email on two accounts)", fails "merge Dana Whitfield and Dana Wu": two different people with a shared first name) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never merge a teammate, an already merged copy, or a pair the owner marked different. **Write:** `contact:merge`
- **Remove a contact** `contact.remove`: Only for a contact that should never have existed (made by mistake, not a person); someone who left is marked inactive instead. **Format:** {action: remove, record: contact, id}; it goes to Trash. (≤80; passes "remove 7d3e1a90 (it-alerts@ mailing list)", fails "remove Lee Park (retired)": mark inactive so the history stays) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never remove a person who took part in a meeting or email. **Write:** `contact:remove`
- **Sentiment to Panzura** `person.sentiment`: How this person feels about Panzura right now and why: the chip on Key people and the first thing to know before a call. **Format:** Positive, neutral or negative first, then why, in one line as of the latest call or email; rewritten whole. (≤300; passes "Positive: says the 8.7.1 upgrade fixed the Revit slowness (Oct 28 call).", fails "Good relationship.": no tone word first and no why) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never the account’s sentiment (green / yellow / red is the owner’s). **Write:** `box.person.sentiment`
- **Background** `person.background`: Career, time at the company, what they own and where they came from: when the title doesn’t say it. **Format:** Two or three sentences, at most 600 characters. (≤600; passes "Eight years at Acme; owns storage, backup and the Panzura filers since 2021. Came from a VAR, so knows the channel.", fails "Very experienced IT professional.": says nothing the owner can use) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → Web → HubSpot. **Never:** Never personal life beyond what they offered. **Write:** `box.person.background`
- **Personality** `person.personality`: How they come across and how to work with them: short answers or long ones, data first or story first. **Format:** Two sentences at most, at most 600 characters. (≤600; passes "Direct and numbers-first; wants the TB and the price before the story. Answers email within a day.", fails "Nice person, a bit grumpy on Tuesday.": one mood, not how to work with them) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a judgement the owner couldn’t repeat to them. **Write:** `box.person.personality`
- **Interests and small talk** `person.interests`: The "you mentioned…" opener: hobbies, family they bring up, teams, trips. **Format:** One per line, with where it came up, at most 300 characters; at most 3 per person per run. (≤300; passes "Coaches his daughter’s soccer team; tournament in Boise in November (Oct 28 call).", fails "Likes sports.": nothing to ask about next time) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never health, religion, politics or anything they’d not want written down. **Write:** `line.person.interests`
- **Sore spots** `person.sore_spots`: What not to raise and what went wrong before, so the owner doesn’t step on it. **Format:** One per line, sourced, at most 300 characters; at most 3 per person per run. (≤300; passes "Still raw about the March outage that took Denver offline for a day; don’t joke about uptime.", fails "Doesn’t like problems.": not specific) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** At most 3 per run. **Write:** `line.person.sore_spots`
- **Observations** `person.observations`: The evidence: one dated, sourced line per thing noticed. **Format:** One line per thing, dated the call or email day, at most 300 characters; 3 to 6 per person per run, never more. (≤300; passes "Said she signs off on the renewal and wants the Dallas quote before the Jan budget meeting.", fails "Was on the call.": not something noticed) **Look:** CodyNote (email references) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** At most 6 per person per run, the first run included: keep the strongest. **Write:** `line.person.observations`
- **Correct one of Claude’s own lines** `person.line_supersede`: A wrong count or a line dated a year off used to become "fix by hand"; Claude now corrects its own lines, the old text kept in Earlier versions. **Format:** {action: supersede, record: line, card, id, fields: {line_id, text?, date?}} with a source. (≤300; passes "line 4e1b: "Six snapshot alerts and three follow-up tickets in October."", fails "line 4e1b (typed by the owner): reworded": the owner’s lines are never rewritten) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never on an owner line. **Write:** `line:supersede`
- **Name a "Speaker N"** `speaker.name`: OneNote transcripts say Speaker 1, Speaker 2: naming them makes every quote and Observation from the call land on the right person. **Format:** {label: "Speaker 2", name, contact_id | teammate_id | is_owner: true}, meeting_id at the top. (≤120; passes "Speaker 2 = Dana Whitfield (contact)", fails "Speaker 3 = probably Sam": a guess) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never a label already named (the owner’s). **Write:** `speaker.label`, `speaker.name`, `speaker.contact_id`
- **Match an attendee to a contact** `attendee.match`: Gives each contact their last met date and puts the call on their profile. **Format:** {meeting_id, contact_id, name_text (the attendee as written)}. (≤120; passes "Dana W. on the Oct 28 sync = Dana Whitfield", fails "Dana = Dana Wu": two Danas on the account; the address shows which) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** The account’s own contacts only (an MSP person is named as a speaker, not matched). **Write:** `attendee.meeting_id`, `attendee.contact_id`, `attendee.name_text`

**Never written by Claude:** Notes on a person (`person.notes`, owner only); Last met and last emailed (`person.last_met`, the app works it out); Email domains (`account.email_domains`, owner only).

## Account row and products (`account`)

Company › Overview: the header, the account row, Products, your sentiment. The account row says whose account it is, how it is grouped and its cloud; Products says which Panzura products were discussed, bought or are live. Most of it changes rarely and only on a clear source.

- **Company name** `company.name`: How the owner and Claude name the account everywhere. **Format:** The company name as HubSpot has it, 1 to 200 characters. (≤200; passes "Acme Engineering", fails "Acme - FY27 Renewal": a deal name, not the company) **Look:** HubSpot (company) → CodyNote. **Never:** Never rename an existing account only to match HubSpot’s style: the owner names accounts. **Write:** `company.name`
- **Account group** `company.account_group`: Current, prospect, new logo, lost or old. **Format:** One of: current, prospect, new_logo, lost, old. (≤8; passes "lost", fails "quiet": not a group) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook → CodyNote. **Never:** Account group, owner and RSM: never, unless a HubSpot or email source says so. **Write:** `company.account_group`
- **Is it my account** `company.is_my_account`: "Accounts get reassigned often." No means the owner is covering for a teammate; the quarter shows it as covering. **Format:** true or false. (≤5; passes "false", fails "yes": true or false only) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook → CodyNote. **Never:** Account group, owner and RSM: never, unless a HubSpot or email source says so. **Write:** `company.is_my_account`
- **Owned by (teammate)** `company.owner_teammate_id`: Which teammate owns the account when it isn’t the owner’s: who to ask before acting. **Format:** A teammate id from codynote_get_customer’s teammates; null clears it. (≤36; passes "5c0e2f71-3a9b-4d2e-9f10-2b7c8d4e6a11", fails "Sam": a name, not a teammate id) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook → CodyNote. **Never:** Account group, owner and RSM: never, unless a HubSpot or email source says so. **Write:** `company.owner_teammate_id`
- **RSM** `company.rsm_teammate_id`: The sales rep paired with the account: who to loop in on an upsell. **Format:** A teammate id; null clears it. (≤36; passes "8a41d3c2-6e7f-4b10-a2c3-9d8e7f6a5b40", fails "the AE": not a teammate id) **Look:** HubSpot → Outlook → CodyNote. **Never:** Account group, owner and RSM: never, unless a HubSpot or email source says so. **Write:** `company.rsm_teammate_id`
- **Managed by (MSP)** `company.managed_by`: The MSP or Panzura partner that runs the account: its people show up on the calls and in Who’s who. **Format:** The managing account’s CodyNote name (or its company id); null clears it. One level only. (≤200; passes "Northwind Partners", fails "Acme Engineering": an account can’t manage itself) **Look:** HubSpot → CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never a partner that isn’t in CodyNote: say it in the reply. **Write:** `company.managed_by`, `company.managed_by_company_id`
- **Primary cloud** `company.primary_cloud`: The main cloud the customer runs Panzura on: the account’s cloud estate, which drives Mirroring and Nexus conversations. **Format:** The cloud as said, up to 100 characters. (≤100; passes "Azure", fails "Azure probably (node names)": a guess) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `company.primary_cloud`
- **Secondary cloud** `company.secondary_cloud`: A second cloud or object store in use (a DR copy, an archive tier): a Mirroring opening. **Format:** As said, up to 100 characters. (≤100; passes "AWS + Wasabi", fails "maybe GCP later": not in use) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `company.secondary_cloud`
- **Last QBR (typed)** `company.last_qbr`: Overrides the newest QBR meeting for the qbr signal and "since the last QBR", for a QBR held outside CodyNote. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2026-09-24", fails "2027-01-15": a planned QBR, not the last one) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot → Outlook. **Never:** Never a future date. **Write:** `company.last_qbr`
- **Last roadmap (typed)** `company.last_roadmap`: Same as the last QBR, for roadmap sessions held outside CodyNote. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2026-06-12", fails "June": not a date) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot. **Never:** Never a future date. **Write:** `company.last_roadmap`
- **Goal: what they want from Panzura this year** `company.goal`: The account’s one sentence: what the customer wants from Panzura this year (owner decision 5, 2026-10-31). **Format:** One sentence, at most 300 characters, in the customer’s terms: the outcome and by when if they said it. (≤300; passes "One file system for every office by the Q1 budget, with Dallas on CloudFS from day one and no new storage hardware.", fails "Upsell 50 TB of Archive.": Panzura’s target, not what the customer wants) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `company.goal`
- **Next meeting** `company.next_meeting_on`: When the owner next meets the customer, so the summary and the book say "next meeting in 3 days: prep" (a signal within 7 days). **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD, today or later. (≤10; passes "2026-11-12", fails "2026-10-02": in the past: that meeting has happened (add it as a meeting instead)) **Look:** Owner → Outlook → Fathom → CodyNote. **Never:** Never a day before today (CodyNote refuses it). **Write:** `company.next_meeting_on`
- **Product status** `product.status`: Which Panzura products the customer has talked about, bought or has live: the coverage map behind "who could use Threat Control?" and the owner’s OneNote product table (Implemented, Discussed). **Format:** discussed, purchased or implemented. (≤11; passes "implemented", fails "discussed": for a product on the current renewal and live: never downgrade bought or live to discussed) **Look:** HubSpot (deals) → CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never downgrade purchased or implemented. **Write:** `product_status.status`
- **Product quantity** `product.quantity`: The quantity presented or discussed (TB, seats, Rings) for a product not on a signed line. **Format:** A number, zero or more, in the product’s unit. (≤12; passes "50", fails "50 TB?": a number only, and not a guess) **Look:** CodyNote (documents, meetings). **Never:** Never copied from a signed line (the deal holds that). **Write:** `product_status.quantity`
- **Product unit** `product.unit`: The quantity’s unit; it follows the product (TB, seat or Ring). **Format:** TB, seat or ring (VM, node, each only on old lines). (≤4; passes "seat", fails "GB": not a unit CodyNote has) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Leave it out to take the product’s own unit. **Write:** `product_status.unit`
- **ARR presented** `product.arr_usd`: the recipe: `codynote_recipe("product.arr_usd")`. **Write:** `product_status.arr_usd`
- **Product notes** `product.notes`: One line on where the product stands on the account ("presented at the QBR, waiting on budget"). **Format:** One line, dated, up to 300 characters (the box holds 2,000; keep it short). (≤300; passes "Presented at the Sep 24 QBR; Dana wants it after the Dallas move.", fails "Threat Control; Search & Audit; Nexus; Edge": a semicolon list of products, not this product’s state) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never a semicolon list. **Write:** `product_status.notes`

**Never written by Claude:** Fiscal year (retired) (`company.fiscal_year`, owner only); Next QBR (retired) (`company.next_qbr`, owner only); Custom fields (`company.custom_fields`, owner only); Your sentiment (green / yellow / red) (`account.sentiment`, owner only); Why (your sentiment) (`account.sentiment_reason`, owner only); Needs a look (`account.needs_a_look`, the app works it out).

## Rings and capacity (`environment`)

Company › Overview › Environment. Each Ring the customer runs, as said on a call or in a ticket, and its managed capacity (MC) readings over time: used near licensed is the expansion signal.

- **Ring name** `ring.name`: One Ring is one CloudFS deployment (its nodes, one object store, one namespace). **Format:** The name the customer uses, or "<Company> <role or site>", 1 to 100 characters. fields.new_ring: true only when a source shows a second Ring. (≤100; passes "Acme Production", fails "Denver node": a node at one site, not a Ring) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never a second Ring when the account’s only Ring has no environment yet: CodyNote turns that add into a change on it (use its ring_id). **Write:** `ring.name`, `ring.new_ring`
- **Ring role** `ring.role`: What the Ring is for. **Format:** production, dr, archive or test; null when not said. (≤10; passes "dr", fails "backup": not one of the four roles (a DR copy is dr)) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Fill only what a call, document or ticket said, as said; never the newest version or a usual setup guessed. **Write:** `ring.role`
- **CloudFS version** `ring.cloudfs_version`: What release they run: upgrades are a standing CSM talking point (8.5 Instant Node, 8.6 geofencing and S3, 8.7.1). **Format:** The version as said, full ("8.5.1", not "8.5"), up to 50 characters. (≤50; passes "8.5.1", fails "latest": not a version) **Look:** HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings, documents) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Fill only what a call, document or ticket said, as said; never the newest version or a usual setup guessed. **Write:** `ring.cloudfs_version`
- **Node count** `ring.node_count`: How many CloudFS nodes (filers) the Ring has: its size across sites, and an Edge or expansion opening. **Format:** A whole number, 0 to 10,000. (≤5; passes "4", fails "4-5": one whole number) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Fill only what a call, document or ticket said, as said; never the newest version or a usual setup guessed. **Write:** `ring.node_count`
- **Object store** `ring.object_store`: Where this Ring’s data lives (the per-Ring fact; the account’s primary cloud is the estate). **Format:** Store and region as said, up to 200 characters. (≤200; passes "Azure Blob (East US)", fails "cloud": says nothing) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Fill only what a call, document or ticket said, as said; never the newest version or a usual setup guessed. **Write:** `ring.object_store`
- **Hypervisor** `ring.hypervisor`: What the nodes run on: it matters for upgrades and support tickets. **Format:** As said, up to 200 characters. (≤200; passes "VMware ESXi 8", fails "virtual": not a hypervisor) **Look:** HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Fill only what a call, document or ticket said, as said; never the newest version or a usual setup guessed. **Write:** `ring.hypervisor`
- **High availability notes** `ring.ha_notes`: How the Ring survives a node or site loss (HA pairs, failover): a Mirroring and DR conversation. **Format:** One or two short sentences, up to 300 characters (the box holds 2,000). (≤300; passes "HA pair at Denver and Dallas; Boise single node.", fails "HA: yes": says nothing about where or how) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Fill only what a call, document or ticket said, as said; never the newest version or a usual setup guessed. **Write:** `ring.ha_notes`
- **Ring notes (hidden)** `ring.notes`: Anything about the Ring’s setup with no box of its own (sites by node). **Format:** Short, undated setup notes, up to 300 characters (the box holds 2,000). (≤300; passes "Denver and Dallas nodes serve engineering; Azure node is the cloud mirror for DR.", fails "Oct 21: upgrade ticket opened; Oct 28: closed; MC 88%.": dated events and a reading: History and MC readings hold those) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never a date list or a reading. **Write:** `ring.notes`
- **Merge two Rings** `ring.merge`: An import once left one Ring with the MC readings and another with the version and nodes; merging moves the readings and fills the blanks. **Format:** {action: merge, record: ring, id: <the Ring to keep>, fields: {merge_ids: [the others]}}. (≤160; passes "merge Ring 2c9e into Ring 81fa (same deployment; one has the readings)", fails "merge Acme DR into Acme Production": two real Rings with different roles) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never merge Rings with different roles or object stores. **Write:** `ring:merge`
- **MC reading date** `mc.recorded_on`: The day the capacity was true: readings over time show growth toward the licence. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2026-10-21", fails "2026-10-31": today, though the alert was on Oct 21) **Look:** HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never today by default. **Write:** `mc_reading.recorded_on`
- **MC used (TB)** `mc.used_tb`: Managed capacity in use. **Format:** TB, a number zero or more, as read (101.17, not 100). (≤12; passes "101.17", fails "100": rounded from 101.17) **Look:** HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings, documents) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never from a summary alone: a transcript, ticket, email or document quote. **Write:** `mc_reading.mc_used_tb`
- **MC licensed (TB)** `mc.licensed_tb`: The licensed capacity the reading was taken against. **Format:** TB, a number, as the reading says. (≤12; passes "125", fails "610": the deals’ CloudFS TB copied in, while the alert said 125 licensed) **Look:** HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never changed to match the deals: when the Rings’ total differs from the current renewals’ CloudFS TB, needs-a-look shows ring_license_mismatch; say both numbers in the reply. **Write:** `mc_reading.mc_licensed_tb`
- **Reading notes (hidden)** `mc.notes`: Where the number came from, in a few words. **Format:** A few words, up to 120 characters (the box holds 2,000). (≤120; passes "Capacity alert ticket 4471", fails "They are growing fast and will need more soon": an opinion, not where the number came from) **Look:** HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never a forecast or opinion. **Write:** `mc_reading.notes`

**Never written by Claude:** MC % and the capacity signal (`mc.percent`, the app works it out).
