## Storylines (`storylines`)

Company › Overview › Storylines (Projects and Issues) and each storyline card. A storyline is one thing going on with the account (a project, an issue, an opportunity, a risk): its one line, where it stands now, what happened (History), the Panzura angle, what we still need to find out, and from 0.48.0 its goal, when it is done, by when, who drives it and the next step.

- **Open a new storyline** `storyline.open`: A storyline is one thing going on with the account that will take more than one call: a project, an issue, an opportunity, a risk. **Format:** add_bullet with section projects (project, opportunity) or issues (issue, risk), kind, the one line, now_text, its first History line and the lines it has. (≤120; passes "projects / opportunity: Dallas office on CloudFS", fails "issues / risk: Dana mentioned Egnyte once": a mention, not yet a storyline: a Signals to watch line on the existing one) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents, email references). **Never:** A new storyline needs a CodyNote meeting, document or email as its source; a HubSpot record alone can’t open one. **Write:** `bullet:add_bullet`, `bullet.section`
- **The one line** `storyline.text`: The storyline’s name on every Overview: what it is about at a glance, so the owner can scan the account in seconds. **Format:** The outcome or problem as a short noun phrase, at most 90 characters, no dates. (≤90; passes "Dallas office on CloudFS", fails "Oct 28: Dana said Dallas opens Feb 1, waiting on IT": dates and status belong in History and Now) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents, email references). **Never:** Never a date in the one line. **Write:** `bullet.text`
- **Kind** `storyline.kind`: Project, issue, opportunity or risk. **Format:** project, issue, opportunity or risk. (≤11; passes "risk", fails "problem": not a kind) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never flipped back and forth: change it when the material changes what it is (an issue that now threatens the renewal is a risk). **Write:** `bullet.kind`
- **Status** `storyline.status`: Open, watch (parked until a date) or resolved (with how it ended): what is live on the account. **Format:** open, watch or resolved. (≤8; passes "resolved", fails "done": not a status) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** watch needs watch_until; resolved needs an outcome. **Write:** `bullet.status`
- **Watch until** `storyline.watch_until`: The day a parked storyline comes back among Open (watch_due flags it). **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD, only with status watch. (≤10; passes "2027-01-12", fails "January": not a date) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never without status watch. **Write:** `bullet.watch_until`
- **Outcome** `storyline.outcome`: How it ended: worked (done, or it went our way), dropped (they stopped, or it went against us), irrelevant (no longer matters). **Format:** worked, dropped or irrelevant, only with resolved. (≤10; passes "worked", fails "won": not an outcome) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never without status resolved. **Write:** `bullet.outcome`
- **Now** `storyline.now`: Where it stands today, the first thing the owner reads on the card. **Format:** Where it stands today, 1-3 sentences (at most 600 characters), rewritten whole. (≤600; passes "Opening Feb 1 with about 40 users; IT is choosing between CloudFS and Egnyte at the Jan 12 budget meeting.", fails "Ongoing; we continue to work with the customer on this.": says nothing about where it stands) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, email references) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never appended to: rewritten whole. **Write:** `bullet.now_text`
- **History line** `storyline.history_text`: The evidence: one dated fact per thing that happened. **Format:** One past-tense sentence, one fact, at most 300 characters. (≤300; passes "IT lead confirmed the Dallas office opens Feb 1.", fails "Dallas opens Feb 1; Egnyte also considered; budget in Jan.": three facts in one line: one line each) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents, email references) → HubSpot (tickets, notes). **Never:** Only added: never reworded, merged or dropped. **Write:** `history.text`, `history.bullet_id`
- **History date** `storyline.history_date`: When it happened: storyline_stale and now_behind read it, so a wrong year skews both. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future. (≤10; passes "2026-10-28", fails "2026-10-31": today, not the call day) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, email references) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never today by default. **Write:** `history.on_date`
- **History source** `storyline.history_source`: Where the fact came from, so the owner can open it. **Format:** {type: meeting | transcript | attachment | link | email | hubspot, id, title, url}; hubspot id <object type>:<id>. (≤200; passes "{type: hubspot, id: ticket:4471, title: Snapshot alerts}", fails "{type: link, title: HubSpot ticket}": a ticket is a hubspot source with its id, not a title-only link) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, email references) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never a source of another account. **Write:** `history.source`
- **Helps** `storyline.helps`: Where Panzura helps with this: the owner’s talking point on the next call. **Format:** One line each, at most 300 characters, sourced. (≤300; passes "Another site on their existing Ring: one file system across offices, no new silo.", fails "Panzura is the best hybrid cloud file system.": a pitch, not tied to this storyline) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Web. **Never:** Every line carries a source with a quote; lines are only added (Claude may supersede its own). **Write:** `line.storyline.helps`
- **Hurts** `storyline.hurts`: Where this works against Panzura or the account: what could lose the renewal or stall the project. **Format:** One line each, at most 300 characters, sourced; a count is exact. (≤300; passes "IT likes that Egnyte needs no hardware in Dallas.", fails "Seven alerts in October.": for six alerts and three follow-up tickets: a count is exact, or it is wrong) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → HubSpot (tickets) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Every line carries a source with a quote; lines are only added (Claude may supersede its own). **Write:** `line.storyline.hurts`
- **Signals to watch** `storyline.signals_to_watch`: What to keep an eye on: a date, a decision, a person, a competitor. **Format:** One line each, at most 300 characters, sourced; a date in it when there is one. (≤300; passes "The Jan 12 budget meeting decides Dallas storage.", fails "Keep watching.": no signal named) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (notes). **Never:** Every line carries a source with a quote; lines are only added (Claude may supersede its own). **Write:** `line.storyline.watch`
- **Open questions** `storyline.open_questions`: What we still need to find out: the owner’s questions for the next call. **Format:** One question per line, ending with "?", at most 300 characters. (≤300; passes "Who decides for Dallas, and by when?", fails "Follow up on Dallas.": a task, not a question) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never removed. **Write:** `line.storyline.open_questions`
- **Tick an answered question** `storyline.tick`: Marks a question answered, with the source that answered it. **Format:** {record: tick, card: storyline, id: bullet_id, fields: {key: open_questions, line_id}} with the answering source. (≤120; passes "tick line 7a2c (Dana decides, by Jan 12)", fails "tick line 7a2c (probably answered)": no source that answers it) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never untick or remove. **Write:** `tick.storyline.open_questions`
- **Goal** `storyline.goal`: What success is for the customer and for Panzura: without it a storyline summary is only the free-text Now. **Format:** One sentence, at most 300 characters: the outcome and why it matters. (≤300; passes "Dallas runs on the existing Ring from day one, so Acme keeps one file system and adds about 20 TB.", fails "Dallas office on CloudFS.": repeats the one line; says nothing about why) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never over a box the owner typed. **Write:** `bullet.goal`
- **Done when** `storyline.done_when`: The concrete end state that resolves it; the verify mode checks against it. **Format:** One checkable sentence, at most 300 characters. (≤300; passes "Dallas users open files from the Ring and the 20 TB upsell is Closed Won.", fails "The customer is satisfied.": not checkable) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never over a box the owner typed. **Write:** `bullet.done_when`
- **Target date** `storyline.target_date`: When it should land (a target, not Watch until’s parking date). **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2027-02-01", fails "Q1": not a date) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never invented. **Write:** `bullet.target_date`
- **Owner (who drives it)** `storyline.owner`: Who drives it (owner, 2026-11-01): a contact at the customer, a teammate, or the owner. **Format:** owner_person_id: a contact of the account (its person_id), a teammate’s id, or "me" for the owner. (≤80; passes "Dana Whitfield (contact)", fails "IT": not a person) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a person not on the account. **Write:** `bullet.owner_person_id`
- **Next step** `storyline.next_step`: The very next action that moves it, so the summary shows what happens next without opening the items. **Format:** One verb phrase, at most 120 characters, with who and when if known. (≤120; passes "Send Dana the 20 TB Collab quote by Nov 6", fails "Follow up": no action anyone can do) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never over a box the owner typed. **Write:** `bullet.next_step`
- **Mentioned in (a source, nothing else)** `storyline.mention`: Records that a call came back to a storyline without anything new, so "still true?" doesn’t ask about it. **Format:** A mention with sources only. (≤80; passes "mention 5f2a: came up on the Oct 28 sync", fails "mention with new text": new facts are History) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** Never changes the text. **Write:** `bullet:mention`
- **Split old Notes into the boxes** `storyline.split`: Old cards kept everything in Notes; a one-time split offers it into the boxes. **Format:** {record: split, card, id, fields: {boxes, lines}}, once per card, no source needed. (≤120; passes "split 5f2a: 2 open questions, 1 Hurts line", fails "split 5f2a again": once per card) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never more than once per card. **Write:** `split.boxes`, `split.lines`
- **Check an open question** `verify.question`: Has the question been answered? **Format:** record verification on the question line’s id: done (evidence) ticks it; still_open, unclear or no_longer_true (the question no longer matters, with a source) note the check. (≤300; passes "done: Dana said the CFO signs, by Dec 15 (meeting, 2026-10-28)", fails "done: answered": no answer and no source) **Look:** CodyNote (open items, meetings, email references) → Fathom (calls not in CodyNote) → Outlook (sent mail, replies) → Teams (chats). **Never:** Never done without proof: no source that shows it, it stays open (still_open, with what was searched). **Write:** `verification.searched`, `verification.checked_on`
- **Check a signal to watch** `verify.watch`: A signal that names a day ("the Jan 12 budget meeting") needs a look once the day passes: needs-a-look shows watch_line_due until a check says what happened. **Format:** record verification on the line’s id: no_longer_true or done with evidence (the line shows settled, it stays), still_open or unclear with a note. (≤300; passes "no_longer_true: the budget meeting moved Dallas to next year (email, 2026-01-13)", fails "no_longer_true: old": age is not evidence) **Look:** CodyNote (open items, meetings) → Fathom (calls not in CodyNote) → Outlook (sent mail, replies) → HubSpot (deals). **Never:** Never done without proof: no source that shows it, it stays open (still_open, with what was searched). **Write:** `verification.note`
- **Check a storyline** `verify.storyline`: Does the storyline’s Now still hold? **Format:** record verification on the storyline’s bullet_id: still_open (it holds; searched, note) | no_longer_true (evidence and now: its Now rewritten, 1-3 sentences) | unclear. Never done: resolving is a bullet change. (≤600; passes "no_longer_true, now: "Dallas moved to next year’s budget; Dana revisits it in the Q1 QBR."", fails "done: finished": a storyline is resolved with its outcome, not closed by a check) **Look:** CodyNote (open items, meetings, email references) → Fathom (calls not in CodyNote) → Outlook (sent mail, replies) → HubSpot (deals). **Never:** Never done without proof: no source that shows it, it stays open (still_open, with what was searched). **Write:** `verification.now`

**Never written by Claude:** Storyline notes (`storyline.notes`, owner only); Pin and order (`storyline.pinned`, owner only); Still true (Keep) (`storyline.still_true`, owner only); Now as of and resolved on (`storyline.dates`, the app works it out).

## Action items (`items`)

Company › Action items, Admin, and each item card. One action item per topic, shown everywhere it belongs (the owner's core OneNote pain). The title is "Topic: what exactly, how much, for whom" (0.53.0) and the Next step (who, what, when) is the gray line under it. Each card opens with Next step and Done when, then the story in three labeled parts (Situation: The ask / Where it stands / Why it matters), then what was said, dated (Context, folded behind a caret); Goal stays on old items until they have a Situation. Waiting tags say who the owner waits on and since when, from any source. Picking (item.pick) says what a meeting, an email or a ticket adds, updates or skips.

- **Picking items (the rule every source uses)** `item.pick`: What becomes an item, what updates one and what is skipped, the same for every source (owner, 2026-11-13: one item per topic; steps from a meeting, an email or Fathom about the same work update that item). **Format:** Fold first: match each thing to an open item by topic (the owner’s topic word, not shared words) and update that item: its Next step (record box), a follow-up (record follow_up), or a Context line (record line) with what was said. A new item only for a new topic, with its title, three-part Situation, Done when and Next step. Every new item or update carries a short verbatim quote as evidence in its sources. More than about five new items from one meeting: fold harder. On every refresh of an account, also bring its open items that do not meet the rules up to them (title, three-part Situation, folds, Next step, follow-ups); a title the owner typed is renamed only when something on record is behind it. (≤160; passes "fold: "Pilot quote: 25 TB NAS ring + 25 Edge users" gets Next step "You send Dana (IT director) the revised quote by Fri"", fails "add "Dana to send the PO" and "Send PO reminder to Dana", one from each Fathom list": one thing twice, and Dana’s task as the owner’s: a follow-up waiting on Dana (IT director) on the topic’s item) **Look:** CodyNote (email references) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never a new item for a topic that has an open item: update that one (its Next step, a follow-up, a Context line). **Write:** `action_item:add`
- **Item text** `item.text`: The item’s name, shown on the company page and on Admin at once ("one action item, shown in both places", the owner’s core OneNote pain). **Format:** "Topic: what exactly, how much, for whom", at most 90 characters (the connector refuses longer; the box holds 2,000). The topic first: 1–4 words, the owner’s short label. After the colon the specifics in plain words: the thing, the amount, for whom (a role or the team, not a bare first name). No leading "do this" verb (the connector refuses "Follow up", "Touch base", "Look into"), no ids, ticket numbers, host names or dates, no "Dana:" prefix. It stays true as steps get done. Before → after: "Send combined quote (25TB new ring + 25 Edge) to Dana" → "Pilot quote: 25 TB NAS ring + 25 Edge users"; "Follow up with Sam re scan numbers" → "Nexus scan count: why nightly scans doubled after the upgrade". An open item whose title fails this is renamed with action change, text (the old title stays in its Earlier versions); a title the owner typed is renamed only when something on record (a meeting, email, ticket or Context line) says what it is: "403 Error" stays as typed until the record does. (≤90; passes "Pilot quote: 25 TB NAS ring + 25 Edge users", fails "Send combined quote (25TB new ring + 25 Edge) to Dana": a step with a "do this" verb and a bare first name: the topic goes first, the step in Next step) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, email references) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** One topic, one item: an open item on the topic gets the update (its Next step, a follow-up, a Context line: recipe item.pick) instead of a new item (CodyNote turns a same-words add into that update; fields.new_item: true only when a source shows it is new). **Write:** `action_item.text`
- **Status** `item.status`: Active, waiting (on someone else) or done. **Format:** active, waiting or done. (≤7; passes "waiting", fails "on_hold": On Hold is waiting) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never done without done_proof. **Write:** `action_item.status`
- **Done proof** `item.done_proof`: What shows an item done, shown on the item. **Format:** {kind: meeting | document | email | hubspot, id, title, url?, date}; hubspot id <object type>:<id>. (≤200; passes "{kind: email, id: AAMkAGI2, title: "Re: Collab quote", date: 2026-10-30}", fails "{kind: meeting, title: "probably on the call"}": no id and no date that shows it) **Look:** Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets) → CodyNote (meetings) → Fathom (calls not in CodyNote). **Never:** Never done without proof: add it open with a Context line saying what was checked. **Write:** `action_item.done_proof`
- **Priority** `item.priority`: P1 most urgent to P4: lists show the most urgent first. **Format:** 1 to 4. (≤1; passes "2", fails "0": 1 to 4 only) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never P1 without the urgency in the source. **Write:** `action_item.priority`
- **Due date** `item.due_date`: Fills Past due, This week and Next week on Admin. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD, set only when the source states or implies it; otherwise left empty. (≤10; passes "2026-11-06", fails "ASAP": not a date) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never invented: no date stated or implied in a source, no due date. **Write:** `action_item.due_date`
- **With teammate** `item.teammate_id`: Whose to-do it is when a teammate took it: Admin’s "Waiting on teammates", grouped by teammate (Sam → Acme → disk usage). **Format:** A teammate id; null: none. (≤36; passes "t1 (Sam Ortiz)", fails "support": not a teammate) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a customer contact. **Write:** `action_item.teammate_id`
- **Deal (a next step for it)** `item.deal_id`: Makes the item one of the deal’s Next steps (the quarter table’s "Awaiting PO", "Set Threat Control demo"). **Format:** One of the company’s deal ids (or a ref); null: none. (≤36; passes "d1", fails "Acme renewal": a name, not an id) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never a deal of another account. **Write:** `action_item.deal_id`
- **Sub-item of** `item.parent_id`: The owner’s lettered sub-items under one company item (up to three levels): steps of one task. **Format:** One of the company’s item ids; three levels at most; set, not cleared. (≤36; passes "i1", fails "an item on another account": must be the company’s) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never more than three levels. **Write:** `action_item.parent_id`
- **Storyline** `item.bullet_id`: Ties the item to the storyline it moves, so the storyline shows its open items. **Format:** One of the company’s storyline ids (or a ref). (≤36; passes "s1", fails "Dallas": not an id) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never a storyline of another account. **Write:** `action_item.bullet_id`
- **From meeting** `item.meeting_id`: Which call it came from: "what came out of the QBR". **Format:** One of the company’s meeting ids (or ref), on the add. (≤36; passes "m2", fails "the QBR": not an id) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Only on the add. **Write:** `action_item.meeting_id`
- **Really a new item** `item.new_item`: Keeps an add an add when it looks like an open item by shared words. **Format:** true, on the add. (≤4; passes "true", fails "yes": true only) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never to force a duplicate. **Write:** `action_item.new_item`
- **Summary** `item.summary`: The executive summary over the item, read first on the card and first in Send this (owner, 2026-11-13: "It should be an executive summary over the action item. **Format:** One or two plain sentences, at most 200 characters, no greeting and no personalization (the same words go to the person in Send this). Rewritten whole as things change, never over a Summary the owner typed. (≤200; passes "Dana needs a quote for the new site’s 25 TB, sized by Jordan, ahead of the March renewal.", fails "Hi Dana, just checking in on the quote!": a greeting, and it says nothing about where things stand) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never a greeting, a sign-off or a question to the reader: it is a summary, and Send this sends it as it is. **Write:** `box.item.summary`, `action_item.boxes`
- **Situation** `item.situation`: The whole story of the item in plain words, so someone who missed the call knows what this is, why it matters and what is next (owner, 2026-11-05: item cards must read cold). **Format:** Always three labeled parts, each its own paragraph (a blank line between them; ¶ marks one in the example) starting exactly "The ask:", "Where it stands:" and "Why it matters:", each 1–3 sentences, at most 1,200 characters in all (owner, 2026-11-13). The ask: what was asked or promised, by whom. Where it stands: what has happened, the latest, who has the next move. Why it matters: what it bears on (the renewal, a deadline, a storyline, a risk). People by name with their role ("Dana (IT director at Acme)", "Sam (our SE)"). Every id, host name, ticket number, version number, product term or acronym explained once in plain words, the first time. Only what the record supports. One sentence of Claude’s own reading is allowed, marked "My read:". (≤1200; passes "The ask: Dana (IT director at Acme) asked on the Oct 28 call for a 50 TB Collab quote for the new Dallas office, which opens in January. ¶ Where it stands: The quote went out Nov 3 with Search & Audit (the file audit add-on), as Dana asked. Dana has not answered; her budget meeting that decides it is Jan 12. ¶ Why it matters: Dallas is the growth in the March renewal. My read: a nudge the week of Dec 1 keeps it on the agenda.", fails "Dana asked for a quote for Dallas. It went out and we are waiting. It matters for the renewal.": no labeled parts and no role for Dana: the three parts start "The ask:", "Where it stands:", "Why it matters:") **Look:** CodyNote → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot. **Never:** Never invents a fact, a date or a quote: everything in it traces to a Context line or a source. **Write:** `box.item.situation`, `action_item.boxes`
- **Context** `item.context`: What was said, by whom, on what date; numbers and deadlines. **Format:** One line per thing, dated, at most 300 characters. (≤300; passes "Dana: price must include Search & Audit for Dallas (Oct 28 call).", fails "Discussed on call.": says nothing) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, email references) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Only added; Claude may supersede its own. **Write:** `line.item.context`, `action_item.lines`
- **Done when** `item.done_when`: The concrete end state: what is true when this is finished. **Format:** One checkable sentence, at most 300 characters (the box holds 600). (≤300; passes "Dana has the 50 TB quote with Search & Audit in her inbox.", fails "Customer happy with pricing.": not checkable) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never over a box the owner typed. **Write:** `box.item.done_when`
- **Next step** `item.next_step`: The one move next so the item moves (who, what, when), shown as the gray line under the title in the items list; if nobody can name it, the item is stuck. **Format:** Who, what, when, at most 120 characters (the box holds 600). Who: "You" (the owner) or a name with role ("Dana (IT director)", "Sam (our SE)"). What: the one move. When: a day ("by Fri Nov 14") or "this week", only when a source says or implies it; otherwise no when. The items list shows it as the gray line under the title; rewritten as the item moves. (≤120; passes "You send Dana (IT director) the 50 TB quote by Fri Nov 14", fails "Send the quote soon": no who, and "soon" is not a when) **Look:** CodyNote → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets) → Fathom (calls not in CodyNote). **Never:** Never replaces an owner-typed Next step. **Write:** `box.item.next_step`
- **Waiting tag: what the owner did** `follow_up.verb`: The owner’s yellow tag "(m Dana 10/21)": messaged, sent, opened (a ticket), called, emailed, met. **Format:** messaged, sent, opened, called, emailed, met or other. (≤9; passes "sent", fails "pinged": not a verb CodyNote has (messaged)) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never on an item that is done. **Write:** `follow_up.verb`, `follow_up.item_id`
- **Waiting on (person)** `follow_up.person`: Who the owner waits on (34 waiting items said on whom only 5 times). **Format:** A name with their role ("waiting on ⟨name, role⟩"), up to 100 characters. (≤100; passes "Dana (IT director)", fails "them": no one named) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never a guess: no source saying it, no value. **Write:** `follow_up.person`
- **Waiting since** `follow_up.occurred_on`: The day of the nudge; several dates make the follow-up history "(m 9/21 10/19)". **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2026-10-21", fails "10/21": not YYYY-MM-DD) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings) → Outlook (email threads) → HubSpot (tickets). **Never:** Never today by default. **Write:** `follow_up.occurred_on`
- **Waiting tag note (hidden)** `follow_up.note`: A short note on the nudge; no screen shows it yet, so keep it to the thing sent. **Format:** A few words, up to 120 characters (the box holds 500). (≤120; passes "Quote v2 with Search & Audit", fails "Hi Dana, following up on…": the email’s text) **Look:** Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never a body. **Write:** `follow_up.note`
- **Waiting tag email** `follow_up.email_id`: Links the tag to the sent email, so the reply check knows the thread. **Format:** A message id or email reference id. (≤1000; passes "AAMkAGI2TG93AAA=", fails "Re: quote": a subject) **Look:** Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Only email the owner asked to read. **Write:** `follow_up.email_id`
- **Move to Waiting** `follow_up.set_waiting`: A nudge usually means the next move is theirs: the item moves to Waiting (default). **Format:** true (default) or false. (≤5; passes "true", fails "wait": true or false only) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never on a done item. **Write:** `follow_up.set_waiting`
- **Got a reply (clear the waits)** `follow_up.got_reply`: Waits looked older than they were even when Claude had read the reply; this clears them as the app’s button does. **Format:** {action: change, record: follow_up, fields: {item_id}} with the reply as the source. (≤120; passes "clear waits on item 3c2e (Dana replied Oct 29)", fails "clear waits (out of office)": an auto-reply is no answer) **Look:** Outlook (email threads) → CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** Never on an item with no open follow-ups. **Write:** `follow_up:change`
- **Fold a duplicate item** `item.fold`: One thing, one item: the kept item gets the other’s Context lines (origin and dates kept) and a History row with the other’s title and boxes; the other goes to Trash marked "Folded into ⟨title⟩". **Format:** One change: {action: merge, record: action_item, company, fields: {keep_id, fold_id}, reason (required: why they are one task), sources}. keep_id is the item that stays (codynote_lookalikes’ keep); fold_id goes into it. (≤200; passes "{action: merge, record: action_item, fields: {keep_id: 3c2e, fold_id: 9a1b}, reason: "Dana’s pricing, asked twice"}", fails "fold "Send quote" into "Book demo"": two different tasks) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Never fold a hold pair without the owner saying so. **Write:** `action_item:merge`
- **Check an action item** `verify.item`: Is the item still open? **Format:** record verification on the item’s id: result done (evidence: the meeting, document, email, Teams message or HubSpot record, dated) | still_open (searched, note) | unclear (note: what would settle it). still_open and unclear are recorded at once, quietly (no suggestion); only done waits for the owner. Never no_longer_true: an item no longer wanted is removed. (≤300; passes "done: email "Collab quote, 50 TB" sent to Dana Oct 30 (evidence email, 2026-10-30)", fails "done: probably sent last week": no proof: no source, no date) **Look:** CodyNote (open items, meetings, email references) → Fathom (calls not in CodyNote) → Outlook (sent mail, replies) → Teams (chats) → HubSpot (everything new). **Never:** Never done without proof: no source that shows it, it stays open (still_open, with what was searched). **Write:** `verification.kind`, `verification.result`, `verification.evidence`

**Never written by Claude:** Goal (retired for Claude) (`item.goal`, owner only); Item notes (`item.notes`, owner only); Present at the QBR (`item.is_present`, owner only); Not on Admin (`item.off_admin`, owner only); One-off list (`item.list`, owner only); Own order (`item.pinned`, owner only); Personal item (`item.personal`, owner only); Item documents and links (`item.attachments`, owner only); Item history and completed date (`item.history`, the app works it out); Last checked (`verify.checked_line`, the app works it out).

## Company facts (`facts`)

Company › Overview › Company facts. Firmographics for sizing and conversation: revenue, people, offices, HQ, industry, founded, website, acquisitions and a fixed set of other facts. Claude fills blanks only, each with a link and a date; the owner's values win.

- **Revenue** `fact.revenue`: Sizing: what the customer can spend and how much headroom an upsell has. **Format:** Amount with its year, "$1.2B (FY25)". Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "$1.2B (FY25)", fails "big": no amount and no year) **Look:** CodyNote → Web → HubSpot (company). **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.revenue`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Employees** `fact.employees`: Sizing and Edge seat potential. **Format:** A number or "about N". Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "about 4,800", fails "lots": not a number) **Look:** CodyNote → Web → HubSpot (company). **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.employees`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Offices** `fact.offices`: Sites are where nodes, Rings and Edge seats go: a new office is an expansion. **Format:** Count and spread, "14 in 6 countries". Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "14 in 6 countries", fails "Denver": one city is HQ, not the offices) **Look:** CodyNote → Web. **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.offices`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **HQ** `fact.hq`: Where the company is run from: time zone and region. **Format:** "City, ST" or "City, Country". Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "Denver, CO", fails "USA": a country is not an HQ) **Look:** CodyNote → Web → HubSpot (company). **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.hq`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Industry** `fact.industry`: Matching to Panzura’s use cases and proof stories ("which AEC customers…"). **Format:** A broad group first, then a few words: AEC, Manufacturing, Media, Healthcare, Government, Education, Financial services, Energy, Retail, Technology or Other, then " – " and the detail (owner, 2026-11-01). Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "AEC – civil engineering", fails "Engineering firm doing roads and bridges": no group first, so a filter misses it) **Look:** CodyNote → Web → HubSpot (company). **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.industry`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Founded** `fact.founded`: Small talk and how established the company is. **Format:** A year. Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "1987", fails "the 80s": not a year) **Look:** CodyNote → Web. **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.founded`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Website** `fact.website`: The company’s main site; email domains are a separate list on Contacts. **Format:** A domain, no https. Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "example.com", fails "https://example.com/about-us": a page, not the domain) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (company) → Web. **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.website`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Acquisitions** `fact.acquisitions`: Acquired companies bring new data, sites and users: a migration or expansion opening (often also an opportunity storyline). **Format:** Names with years, newest first. Up to 200 characters (the box holds 1,000). (≤200; passes "Northwind Design (2025), Contoso Survey (2023)", fails "growing by acquisition": no names) **Look:** CodyNote → Web. **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.acquisitions`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Other fact (fixed labels)** `fact.other`: A short list of other facts worth having. **Format:** field other, label one of the allowed six, value up to 200 characters. (≤200; passes "fiscal year end: June 30", fails "notable projects: Denver airport expansion": not an allowed label; a project is a storyline) **Look:** CodyNote → Web. **Never:** Blanks only: a fact the owner set is never replaced (say in the reply when research disagrees); a change only over one Claude set, with a fresher source. **Write:** `fact.other`, `fact.label`, `fact.field`, `fact.value`
- **Fact source (title and link)** `fact.source`: Lets the owner check the number in one click. **Format:** A page title up to 300 characters and its https link. (≤300; passes "Acme Engineering: About us (https://example.com/about)", fails "Google": not the page it came from) **Look:** Web → HubSpot (company). **Never:** Never a link that doesn’t show the value. **Write:** `fact.source_title`, `fact.source_url`
- **Fact as of** `fact.as_of`: When the value was true; fact_old flags a changing fact over a year old. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2026-10-28", fails "2025": not a date) **Look:** Web. **Never:** Never in the future. **Write:** `fact.as_of`

## Knowledge and notes (`knowledge`)

Company › Overview › Tech stack, Workloads / business units, Use cases, Notes. The customer's environment around Panzura in short bullets: what else they run, which parts of the business use it, what they use it for. Notes at the bottom are the owner's scratch pad.

- **Tech stack bullet** `knowledge.tech_stack`: What else they run around Panzura: a competitor to displace (Egnyte, NetApp), an integration to protect (Veeam, Microsoft 365), a Symphony or Nexus opening. **Format:** A product or vendor plus its role, at most 60 characters. (≤60; passes "Egnyte – external sharing with clients", fails "Egnyte": no role: why it matters is unknown) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents, email references). **Never:** At most 8 suggestions per section per scan, imports included; never padding. **Write:** `bullet.text`, `bullet.section`, `bullet:add_bullet`
- **Workloads / business units bullet** `knowledge.workloads`: Which parts of the business and which workloads sit on Panzura: where growth comes from, and who to meet. **Format:** A business unit or workload, with its size if said, at most 60 characters. (≤60; passes "Engineering (6 offices, Revit and Civil 3D)", fails "Various teams": names nothing) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** At most 8 suggestions per section per scan, imports included; never padding. **Write:** `bullet.text`, `bullet.section`, `bullet:add_bullet`
- **Use case bullet** `knowledge.use_cases`: What they use Panzura for, matched to Panzura’s proof stories at a QBR. **Format:** A verb phrase, at most 90 characters. (≤90; passes "Global file locking across six offices", fails "Could use Nexus for Copilot": a possibility, not a use: an opportunity storyline) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents). **Never:** At most 8 suggestions per section per scan, imports included; never padding. **Write:** `bullet.text`, `bullet.section`, `bullet:add_bullet`
- **Knowledge bullet details** `knowledge.details`: The rest of the facts behind a short bullet, in the customer’s words, plus linked research about the technology. **Format:** Short paragraphs, at most 1,500 characters, below the owner’s own details. (≤1500; passes "Used by the design team to share drawings with clients (Oct 28). Research: Egnyte is a cloud file service; overlap with CloudFS is external sharing.", fails "Egnyte is a leading enterprise content platform trusted by thousands.": marketing copy, no customer fact, not labelled) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → Web. **Never:** Never on a storyline (its details are the owner’s Notes). **Write:** `bullet.details_text`, `bullet:add_details`
- **Update, mention or retire a bullet** `knowledge.update`: Newer material wins: a better wording or new facts (update), only came up again (mention), or no longer true (outdated, with the call and a reason). **Format:** update (bullet_id, text and/or details), mention (bullet_id, sources), outdated (bullet_id, reason, text empty to remove). (≤200; passes "outdated 2b4c: "moved backups from Veeam to Rubrik" (Oct 28)", fails "outdated 2b4c: no reason": outdated needs the reason and the newer call) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings). **Never:** A storyline that is over is resolved, not outdated. **Write:** `bullet:update`, `bullet:mention`, `bullet:outdated`

**Never written by Claude:** Overview notes (`knowledge.notes`, owner only); Pin and keep (`knowledge.pinned`, owner only).

## The read (`read`)

Company › Overview › The read, the strip, the scan. Claude's evidence-based read of the account: the one thing to do (Do first) and the account in plain words (Situation, 0.52.0), then five short lines; last in every update and only when something material changed. The owner's own sentiment sits beside it and is theirs alone.

- **Read: Do first** `read.do_first`: The one thing to do on the account and why, first on the Overview (owner, 2026-11-07: "focus first"). **Format:** One sentence, at most 300 characters: the one thing to do and why, then "Then: …" with the next two, each citing its item or storyline by id in brackets (the first 8 characters). (≤300; passes "Send Dana the Dallas quote [3f2a9c1d] this week: the Jan 12 budget meeting decides it. Then: close the slowness ticket [7b10e2aa]; book the Q1 EBR [9c41d0ee].", fails "Keep engaging and follow up on open items.": no one thing, no why, nothing cited) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.do_first`
- **Read: Situation** `read.situation`: The account in plain words, so someone who has never opened it knows who they are, where the renewal stands, what is open and where the openings are (owner, 2026-11-07: the account page must read cold). **Format:** Two or three short paragraphs (a blank line between them; ¶ marks one in the example), at most 1,500 characters in all, in this order: who they are and how they use Panzura; where the renewal stands; what is open and who owes what; the openings. Storylines and items cited by id in brackets (the first 8 characters). One sentence of Claude’s own reading is allowed, marked "my read". (≤1500; passes "Acme is a 400-person engineering firm on CloudFS (the Panzura file system) across three offices, 120 TB licensed, with Search & Audit added last year. ¶ The renewal ends Mar 31; the renewal opp [5d0e77a1] is in Proposal, flat, and Dallas (a fourth office opening in January) would add about 20 TB [3f2a9c1d]. ¶ Open: Dana owes a decision on the Dallas quote after the Jan 12 budget meeting; we owe a fix on the Revit slowness ticket [7b10e2aa], six weeks old. My read: the ticket colours the renewal more than the price does.", fails "Healthy account, renews in March, a few open items.": says nothing someone cold could act on, cites nothing) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.situation`
- **Health** `read.health_level`: Claude’s evidence-based health of the account: healthy, watch or at risk. **Format:** healthy, watch or at_risk. (≤8; passes "watch", fails "yellow": the owner’s sentiment colours, not health) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.health`
- **Read: Health and why** `read.health`: Why the health is what it is, in a line. **Format:** One or two sentences, at most 200 characters, citing the storyline or item it summarises by its id in brackets (the first 8 characters, like [3f2a9c1d]): the executive summary links each one. (≤200; passes "Watch: engaged on calls, but the Revit slowness ticket [3f2a9c1d] is 6 weeks old (my read: it colours the renewal).", fails "Healthy account.": no why) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.health`
- **Read: Renewal** `read.renewal`: When it renews, what’s on the table and how it looks. **Format:** One or two sentences, at most 200 characters, citing the storyline or item it summarises by its id in brackets (the first 8 characters, like [3f2a9c1d]): the executive summary links each one. (≤200; passes "Renews Mar 31; renewal opp in Proposal, flat on 120 TB.", fails "Renewal coming up.": no date, no state) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.renewal`
- **Read: What’s changing** `read.changing`: What moved since the last read: new sites, people, plans. **Format:** One or two sentences, at most 200 characters, citing the storyline or item it summarises by its id in brackets (the first 8 characters, like [3f2a9c1d]): the executive summary links each one. (≤200; passes "New Dallas office opening in Q1; IT lead says file shares there are "the plan".", fails "Nothing much.": say "no change since <date>" instead) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.changing`
- **Read: Risks and openings** `read.risks`: The top risk and the top opening, from the risk and opportunity storylines and their Hurts and Helps. **Format:** One or two sentences, at most 200 characters, citing the storyline or item it summarises by its id in brackets (the first 8 characters, like [3f2a9c1d]): the executive summary links each one. (≤200; passes "Risk: Egnyte came up as an option for Dallas. Opening: MC at 88% of licensed before Dallas.", fails "Some risk.": names nothing) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.risks`
- **Read: The one thing to do next** `read.next`: The single next action for the account, usually the top item’s Next step. **Format:** One or two sentences, at most 200 characters, citing the storyline or item it summarises by its id in brackets (the first 8 characters, like [3f2a9c1d]): the executive summary links each one. (≤200; passes "Get the slowness ticket closed and a capacity quote for Dallas before the Jan budget meeting.", fails "Keep engaging.": no action) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.next`
- **Read as of** `read.as_of`: When the read was true: read_behind flags it when a newer meeting exists. **Format:** YYYY-MM-DD. (≤10; passes "2026-10-28", fails "2026-10-01": older than the Oct 28 call it uses) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.as_of`
- **Scan coverage (and when to stop)** `scan.coverage`: One entry per work-order step (read material, email, people, account, deals, storylines, items, facts, knowledge, read), so nothing is skipped silently; the owner sees it on the scan’s card. **Format:** {read_material, email, people, account, deals, storylines, items, facts, knowledge, read}: each a count, "nothing new", "skipped: <why>" or (email) "not asked". (≤400; passes "people 4 · email not asked · deals nothing new · storylines 3 · items 2 · facts skipped: no web access · read 1", fails "people 4 · storylines 3": steps missing: the read is refused) **Look:** CodyNote. **Never:** Stop only when the brief has no new material and the owner named nothing to work from; a call, email or document the owner names is the material: work every step from it. **Write:** `close_scan.coverage`
- **Summary: why (the read’s health line)** `summary.why`: The narrative beside the health in the executive summary: the read’s Health line, with the storylines and items it rests on cited by id so the summary links them. **Format:** One or two sentences, at most 200 characters, each storyline or item named with its id in brackets (first 8 characters). (≤200; passes "Watch: the Dallas file shares [3f2a9c1d] wait on a quote, and the slowness ticket [7b10e2aa] is 6 weeks old.", fails "Watch: some issues are open.": names nothing and cites no storyline or item) **Look:** CodyNote → HubSpot (deals, tickets). **Never:** One read per scan, in close_scan.read, only when something material changed; accepted only with complete coverage. **Write:** `read.lines.health`
- **Summary: a storyline’s line** `summary.storyline_line`: Each storyline in one line: Goal · status · Now (first sentence) · next step · target date · owner · money · last moved · open questions, computed from its boxes. **Format:** Follow storyline.text (the one line, at most 90 characters, no dates) and storyline.goal (one sentence, at most 300). (≤300; passes "Dallas runs on the existing Ring from day one, so Acme keeps one file system and adds about 20 TB.", fails "Open · moved Oct 28 · 2 questions": the computed part, typed into a box) **Look:** CodyNote (meetings, documents) → Outlook (email threads). **Never:** Never over a box the owner typed. **Write:** `bullet.text`, `bullet.goal`

**Never written by Claude:** Older reads (`read.versions`, owner only); The strip tiles (`read.strip`, the app works it out); Executive summary (computed rows) (`summary.account`, the app works it out).
